about: What a bot of the match can do, and why it would (T67): each action's weight and its considerations, for ActionChoice -- and, weighed the same way after the action, how it holds its body (postures: stand or crouch). A consideration reads one percept MatchBot.numbers_of names -- ready_to_fire, shot_worth, rounds_left, has_reserve, could_fire, enemy_in_sight, in_retreat_wave, to_go (metres), heard; and for the postures moving, shooting, reloading (what the action chose), cover (1 at low cover, 0.5 at high, 0 none) and danger (1 an enemy in sight, else the loudest shot heard or the nearest enemy remembered, by closeness) -- through a line (slope times it, plus intercept, clamped to 0 and 1) or a step (above from at up, below under it). The score is the weight times every answer; the highest is done. Change these and the bot weighs differently; no line of code says which action comes first.
